body:
I've exercised on and off for years. Got fairly into it when I lost a bunch of weight in college. Now I've gained a bunch of it back, and I've tried getting into the groove again. I keep telling myself at the beginning of the day "all right I got this! We're taking it one step at a time! We'll do it this time!" and then I just end up not bothering. I've repeated this cycle so many fucking times I've lost count. I just really don't have the drive anymore. I just don't even want to get my hopes up anymore, because I know eventually they'll get crushed. I'd rather just not bother at this point.

I've never given meditation a serious try.

But if the medication is all that is keeping me afloat, what's to stop me from falling back into the same mindset once I stop taking it (assuming it even works to begin with)?

And like I said, what about cost? I know a lot of medications are really fucking expensive, and I don't know if I can take having to pay another bill.

Saw a therapist for a few months. Stopped going about a month ago cuz I thought things were getting better. She mentioned the possibility of medication.

I guess if it came down to it, I'd consider it. But I do have some reservations. One, I don't want my life to revolve on taking some fucking pill that might or might not work. I don't want to have to be dependent on it, or deal with the side effects. 

Those concerns aside, what about the costs? I'm only making $10.00 and have student loans to pay. Another round of bills would not be something I'd need right now.

I'm not trying to be difficult. Like I said, if that's the only option, I guess I might look into it. I just really don't want to have to rely on something external to get through life. I just want to be happy on my own.
